newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Super Touring Car champion Brad Jones led from the start to win both races in the fourth round of the series at Amaroo Park yesterday. Jones is third in the championship on 72 points, trailing Paul Morris first on 94, and Geoff Brabham second on 92 points. Page 26.

Super League executive director Ian Frykberg said yesterday his competition would only be prepared to consider joint control of rugby league if Australian Rugby League chief sponsor Optus Communications gave a commitment to continue funding in the long term. Optus has only committed funding for the next two years. Page 32.

The Dandenong Rangers defeated the Australian Institute of Sport 67-46 in the women's national basketball league in Canberra yesterday to remain fourth in the competition, assuring them of a place in the semi-finals. The final spot in the semi-finals will be decided between Brisbane, Perth and Canberra next week. Page 27.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The semi-final positions in the national netball league have been thrown open by a weekend of upsets which saw the Adelaide Thunderbirds defeat the previously unbeaten Melbourne Phoenix 67-54, to trail the league leaders by just one point. Page 26. --

The Commonwealth Bank is waiting on a report into a brawl at a soccer match between Tamworth High School and Hurstville High School last Thursday before deciding whether it will continue to sponsor the New South Wales State-wide Commonwealth Bank Cup. TheBank ended its sponsorship of Queensland schoolboy rugby league earlier this year after an on-field brawl. Page 30.

Australian Wallabies coach Greg Smith last night announced Michael Brial would replace Troy Coker while Richard Harry and Andrew Heath would be the new props for Saturday night's Tri Nations rugby union Test against the New Zealand All Blacks. Page 31.
THE AGE

Sydney Swans forward Tony Lockett will face the Australian Football League Tribunal tonight charged with wrestling West Coast Eagle Fraser Gehrig during Saturday night's game. Although wrestling usually results in a fine, a suspension could be handed downbecause of Lockett's poor record at the Tribunal. Page 3.

St George's Jamie Ainscough scored a field goal 12 minutes from full-time in yesterday's Australian Rugby League game against South Sydney at Kogarah Oval to break a 28-all deadlock and give the Dragons the game by one point, 29-28, after leading 24-6 at alf-time. Page 14.

Matt Dunn, 23, broke the Australian all-comers record in the 200 metres individual medley at the Australian short-course swimming championships last night. Dunn swam the event at the Victorian State Swim Centre in 1:57.05, the second-fastest time in the wrld this year. Page 19.
THE HERALD SUN

United Kingdom horse Always Aloof has been named as the first long-shot Melbourne Cup competitor to the surprise of bookmakers. The horse has been in Australia since March and is being trained by Lee Freedman. Page 78.

Defending Australian Open squash champion and world number 10 Brett Martin lost his title to Rodney Eyles in Adelaide yesterday. The 15-9 11-15 17-15 15-17 17-15 finals win gave world number three Eyles his first national title. Page 82.

Recently retired Carlton player Justin Madden plans to lodge a Supreme Court writ against the Australian Football League claiming he is entitled to long service leave, but AFL communications manager Tony Peek dismissed Madden's claims, saying the AFL was ot the employer of the players. Page 86.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Parramatta Eels won their tenth successive Australian Rugby League game, in front of 20,148 fans, yesterday defeating Newcastle 28-22 at Parramatta Stadium. The Eels will play reigning premiers Manly on Friday. Page 33.

South Sydney president George Piggins said yesterday strict financial restraints had to be placed on rugby league clubs if the game was going to survive into the future. Piggins called for rules on how much clubs could spend and for salary caps, with penalties, including expelling the club. Page 45.

The privatisation of the New South Wales TAB next year could mean bookmakers prices become freely available to off-course betters, as tax reform makes the on-course and off-course dollar approximately equal to the value of a race club dollar. Page 47.
